answer: To resist sybils%2C each agent identity must recompute a unique computational anchor every epoch%3A a puzzle formed from its private key plus the prior epoch hash%2C solved against an ocean of fresh random challenges issued by a rotating raven-auditor quorum. The solution is non-transferable and non-amortizable across keys. A farm of N identities therefore expends N independent core-hours%3B any reused solve is flagged as non-unique and the identity is slashed. An honest single agent pays one solve%3B scaling the attack requires scaling the compute linearly.
